newsitem.title: USA: BellSouth, IBM in pact to extend Internet coverage.
newsitem.headline: BellSouth, IBM in pact to extend Internet coverage.

text.p: BellSouth Corp. and International Business Machines Corp. said Wednesday they agreed to an alliance that will allow BellSouth to signficantly expand the Internet access services it provides its customers.
BellSouth said it plans to use IBM's high-capacity private computer network to expand the number of cities where it offers Internet access services to 44 from its current 14.

"Our agreement with IBM will enable BellSouth to provide our Internet services to more than 70 percent of our customer base regionwide," said John Robinson, president of BellSouth.net, the carrier's Internet access service.
"This positions BellSouth to be the leading Internet service provider in the Southeast," he said.

Besides extending BellSouth's capacity to offer Internet services within the nine-state region of the southeast United States where it provides local phone service, the IBM Global Network also provides BellSouth customers with Internet access while travelling in other U.S. regions and overseas.
In addition, the two companies said they were working together to develop a new high-speed network capable of handling intranet and Internet traffic.
Intranets are private networks operated by individual companies.

This future high-capacity network would take advantage of technologies capable of sending millions of bits of data per second over standard phone lines and provide a secure way to conduct financial transactions over the Internet, they said.
BellSouth.net has signed up tens of thousands of subscribers since it was introduced last fall and is projecting hundreds of thousands of customers by the end of 1997, a spokesman said.

An official at IBM's network services unit said the partnership with BellSouth was an early example of how IBM planned to work with local phone companies in the United States and around the globe to develop an enhanced set of Internet services on top of the IBM Global Network.
The IBM Global Network, one of the world's largest private computer networks, is used mainly mainly by corporations to provide high-capacity links to offices around the world.
